content.text:
A violent flood transforms the dry countryside, destroying bridges and isolating communities while intensifying romantic tensions. Gertrude realizes she loves Burt but fears betraying Amy; Amy releases Burt from his former promise, and he successfully declares his love to Gertrude. Webb patiently wins Amy’s heart, and they become engaged at Christmas. Their families celebrate, help reform Lumley, and comfort the troubled Alvord.

A second narrative follows Jose de Rincon, a conflicted Spanish priest. His journal exposing doubts about Catholic doctrine and Vatican politics is lost in a Roman park, published, and used against him. Summoned before the Pope, Jose refuses to recant and is declared insane, then confined to a monastery. Later sent to Cartagena, he is assigned to Simiti but meets American explorer Amos Hitt, whose radical Christian ideas inspire Jose to question ecclesiastical authority and seek truth.
